# Sheet 2: static timing at the final pin assignment (gate G-STA)

**Run:** 2026-11-19 on the owner's PC with Lattice Diamond 3.14.0.75.2 (free licence): LSE synthesis, map, PAR and TRACE.

**Command:** `bash hdl/syn/run_diamond.sh <work dir> <device>`. For the fit test, set `Z2_TOP=fit_top`.

**Pins:** fixed by the LOCATE block in [../../hdl/syn/z2_top.lpf](../../hdl/syn/z2_top.lpf), generated by `tools/fpga/pinplan.py`. The fit test also uses [../../hdl/syn/fit_top_extra.lpf](../../hdl/syn/fit_top_extra.lpf), which holds the 16 ports of sheets 4–6 and ZB_E7M. The LPF of every run below is byte-identical to the committed file.

**RTL:** unchanged since sheet 3 rev A1, which passed `run_checks.sh`.

> **What this closes and what it does not.**
> - **Closes:** the "final pin assignment and STA including the complete /SLAVEn path" part of G-STA (owner open requirement 1): every Zorro path at the real pins on both grades.
> - **Still open:** G-STA as a whole. The host SPI capture path is analysed once the SPI slave exists (sheet 4, HL-1 to HL-6), and the figures still have to be compared with M-1, M-2 and M-7 on hardware.

## 1. Conditions

Unchanged from [sheet1-sta-results.md](sheet1-sta-results.md) §1, except that the pins are now fixed.

- **Grades:** −4, commercial (TJ 85 °C) and industrial (TJ 100 °C; map `-oc Industrial`, confirmed in the map report).
- **Loads:** 15 pF on every output.
- **I/O:** LVCMOS33 on every port.
- **Edges:** both rising and falling.
- **Minimum delays:** from the fast model.

**Pad check:** passed on every run (every port LVCMOS33, every used bank at VCCIO 3.3 V). The check fails the script otherwise; that rule came out of the PR #3 correction.

**Worst Zorro path: 15.094 ns** (A16 → /SLAVEn and A16 → XRDY, industrial). That is 2.906 ns inside the 18 ns allocation. The exploratory sheet-1 run with Diamond-placed pins gave 15.311 ns.

**Utilisation:** 434 of 1056 slices (41 %); 404–412 of 2112 registers.

## 4. Hazard inequality (C-02), M-7 pass criterion and tracked margins

The buffer-skew term is 3.5 ns, as in sheet 1 §4.

| Requirement | Conservative (slow max − fast min, across all runs) | Same corner (slow), worst run |
|---|---|---|
| **Slot address setup S_req** | 3.5 + (15.094 − 2.355) = **16.24 ns** | 3.5 + (15.094 − 8.849) = **9.75 ns** (z2_top I) |
| Slot address hold | 3.5 + (8.882 − 2.782) = **9.60 ns** | – |

- **M-7 pass criterion:** measured slot setup **≥ 19.2 ns** (16.24 + 3). The sheet-1 exploratory value was 19.4 ns.
  - A result between 12.8 and 19.2 ns is acceptable only on the same-corner basis, and must be recorded as such.
  - **Hold:** 9.6 ns is needed; the MC68000 gives ≥ 40 ns (#13) [V S57].
- **R-43 (50 MHz):** worst slack 3.92 ns, the trigger being 1 ns. Rev A1 showed 3.66–4.76 ns with Diamond-placed pins.
- **R-41 / M-12 (PiStorm/Emu68):** any master must give slot setup ≥ 19.2 ns, or ≥ 12.8 ns on the same-corner basis.

| ZB_A[23:16] → ZF_SLAVE_N, slowest | 18 | 13.546 (A16) | **15.850 (A18)** |
| ZB_A[23:16] → ZF_XRDY, slowest | 18 | 13.546 | 15.453 |
| → ZF_DBUF_OE_N, slowest (/LDS) | 18 | 14.890 | 13.836 |
| ZB_CFGIN_N → ZF_CFGOUT_N | 25 | 10.941 | 11.350 |
| 50 MHz slack | ≥ 0 | 4.842 | **3.601** |
| Clock-to-out SRAM_OUT / LD_OUT (max) | 12 / 16 | 9.879 / 12.749 | 9.879 / 12.527 |
| /SLAVEn at the slot | 35 | 20.43 ns | 20.62 ns |
| S_req conservative (both runs) / M-7 criterion | – | 16.71 ns / **≥ 19.7 ns** | |
| Utilisation | – | 434 of 2160 slices (20 %) | |

**The fallback meets every constraint at these pins**, with about 0.5–0.8 ns less margin on the slowest bits than the 2000HC.

**If the 4000HC is bought:**
- rerun the industrial grade;
- use the 4000's figures for M-7 (≥ 19.7 ns on these runs).

## 6. Warnings

Same set as sheet 1 §6 and sheet 3: ZB_E7M has no load; `ld_dout` initial values are ignored; the asgate VCC/GND nets have no load; there is no .sdc file. The sheet-3 synthesis also reports registers stuck at constant values in the host path (`hr_ack`, `h_irq_n`, `own_h`). That is expected while `z2_hostif_stub` ties the host port off.

**No new warning class.** The Diamond log warnings were compared by message class, with numbers and names normalised, against the rev A1 runs (Diamond-placed pins). All six runs have 0 new classes.
